transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-15
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 00:47:00
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Lin (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Atlas PM), Ravi Patel (Atlas ML Eng), Sophie Chen (Atlas Infra)

Summary:
Quick weekly sync to review recent pilot runs, decide on model pinning strategy, and define an emergency swap (fast rollback) plan. Customer wants clear RTO for cutover to fallback model and proof that fallback won't blow cost budgets. Discussed hosted vs dedicated implications and VPC/KMS concerns.

Topics:
- recent throughput/latency runs (redwood-14b-quant vs redwood-7b-quant)
- pinning semantics: soft pin (traffic weighting) vs hard pin (version lock)
- emergency swap: automated routing vs manual cutover and required SLAs
- security/residency notes for VPC and key management

Transcript body:
[00:00:12] Ethan: Hey all, thanks for joining. quick agenda — run results, pin policy decision, and walk through emergency swap. Maya is going to run through numbers.
[00:00:28] Maya: cool, yeah i pulled the last 48 hours from the pilot. we did a mixed workload: 65% short prompts, 35% long reasoning. redwood-14b-quant averaged 180ms p50, 640ms p95, but that p95 spikes correlated with cold kv cache, so we did a warmup patch mid-run. some of the samples are noisy cause the infra was doing node rebuilds earlier.
[00:00:53] Ravi: quick q — is that 640ms at our 512 token config or full 1k?
[00:01:01] Maya: those numbers are at 512 token average. at 1k it went to about 900ms p95 in our run windows. also note the 7b-quant was about 110ms p50, 420ms p95. cost per token for 14b is around 2.7x of 7b in our setup because of seq length and kernel choices.
[00:01:26] Liam: so we're balancing latency vs quality — we saw quality lift on multi-step answers with 14b in evals, but it wasn't huge for all prompts. can we soften degrade gracefully?
[00:01:40] Maya: yes, that's where soft-pin and shadowing helps. we can do traffic weight 80/20 (primary/backup) and shadow 100% to collect outputs. soft-pin means routing prefers pinned version but still allows fallback if capacity constrained. hard-pin is pinned and locked — no automatic fallback.
[00:02:05] Sophie: what's the emergency swap flow? our SREs want a <5min RTO for customer-facing endpoints.
[00:02:12] Ethan: two options: automated policy-based swap that reroutes by model family on health signals (latency/slo breaches) or manual cutover initiated by Atlas on-call. automated can be 10-30s to shift if using the routing layer, but you need to accept brief partial outputs; manual is slower but safer.
[00:02:34] Ravi: does automated swap keep same request fidelity? will it map completions from 14b to 7b seamlessly?
[00:02:41] Maya: semantic differences remain; you can configure escape hatch to change prompt prefix or increase sampling temp to keep behavior similar. Also important: KV cache warmup — when you swap down to 7b it won't share kv cache, so first N requests may be slower.
[00:03:02] Ethan: also note we can do model-variant alignment — deploy a 14b-compat quant that is tuned to match 7b latency, so the swap delta is smaller. but that takes onboarding time.
[00:03:18] Liam: cost question — if we do automated fallback, will costs spike because of doubled shadow traffic?
[00:03:25] Maya: shadowing adds overhead; in our pilot we did 100% shadow for two days and saw an extra 35% egress compute. we can sample shadowing 20% and still gather quality signal.
[00:03:38] Sophie: security — if we need to swap across regions for capacity, we need to ensure keys stay in our KMS and logs meet sock two and ISO requirements. is that supported in hosted mode?
[00:03:50] Ethan: hosted has region-level options and we can integrate with customer KMS via our private tenant pipeline for Dedicated or Private. for Hosted we offer envelope encryption and bring-your-own-key integrations in certain regions; not all regions yet. note: our compliance docs will call out SOC 2 and ISO 27001 for hosted.
[00:04:15] Ravi: there's a few transcription errors in earlier notes — when you say "K V cash" i think you mean kv cache, just flagging.
[00:04:23] Maya: ya, the auto notes sometimes flop acronyms.
[00:04:29] Liam: okay back to pinning — can we do conditional pinning per route? e.g., pin model A for inference route /cart and model B for /recs?
[00:04:38] Maya: yes per-route pinning is supported, and you can set fallback policies per-route. you can also set a global fallback for the entire customer. routing can be region aware, cost-aware, or latency-aware — you pick the policy.
[00:04:55] Sophie: we like the idea of per-route because cart has stricter latency needs.
[00:05:02] Ethan: proposed approach: pin 14b for /recs where quality matters, soft-pin 14b for /cart with 80/20 fallback to 7b, and schedule a weekly roll-forward window for pin reviews.
[00:05:15] Ravi: what about rollback — can we automate rollback to previous model version if eval regressions appear?
[00:05:22] Maya: we have a version gateway — you can set a canary traffic slice and tie it to quality metrics (bleu-like or custom eval). if the canary drops below threshold we auto-roll back to previous stable version. that's what we did in the demo last month. caveat: automatic rollback needs the previous version still deployed and available.
[00:05:43] Liam: does that require extra reserved capacity? like keep previous versions warm?
[00:05:48] Maya: ideally yes — we recommend a small standby pool or cold start warmers to keep KV cache seeded for the previous version. without warmers, rollback is functional but slower. cost tradeoff vs RTO.
[00:06:06] Ethan: for emergency swap we recommend two options: 1) standby locked fallback — keep 7b pinned on a small reserved capacity pool (warm) for instant swap; cost = reserved. 2) cold fallback with warmers — cheaper but RTO may be minutes.
[00:06:24] Sophie: our budget boundaries: we can accept up to +15% infra cost for standby in peak months, otherwise prefer warmers.
[00:06:31] Ravi: what about model catalog naming? i want clarity so our CI can refer to stable identifiers not friendly aliases.
[00:06:38] Maya: we expose model identifiers and semantic tags. e.g., redwood-14b-quant:v1.3-stable. you can pin by id. we also expose compatible model variants list for automated fallback mapping.
[00:06:54] Liam: any gotchas with private deployments? we may need on-prem V P C and H S M integration.
[00:07:01] Ethan: Private supports HSM/KMS and air-gapped options. note that some runtime optimizations require specific CUDA drivers; our private installer includes kernel checks. for V P C peering we keep control plane in Redwood but can allow private egress to your subnets.
[00:07:20] Sophie: SSO — our compliance folks want SAML and RBAC. do you support SCIM?
[00:07:26] Maya: yes SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning are available for enterprise tiers. RBAC supports route-level roles.
[00:07:34] Liam: let's define concrete thresholds for auto-swap: p95 > 1.2s for 5 minutes triggers a health breach?
[00:07:42] Maya: that's reasonable. we usually set rolling window 5min and require consecutive windows to avoid flapping. can set suppression and cooldown.
[00:07:52] Ethan: i'll capture that as part of runbook.
[00:07:56] Liam: on rollback testing, we want a dry run — simulate swap in staging with traffic replay and measure time to stable. can you provide the tooling?
[00:08:04] Maya: yes we have a traffic-replay harness and tracing hooks. we'll share the harness repo link and instructions.
[00:08:12] Ethan: OK quick alignment on pins today: Atlas will soft-pin 14b for /cart at 80/20 and hard-pin 14b for /recs. Standby: keep a warm 7b pool in region us-west-2 with RTO target 3 minutes.
[00:08:26] Ravi: 3 minutes seems fine. but if the automated swap is possible in 30s we may prefer that — is warming 7b going to block compute for other tenants?
[00:08:34] Maya: on Dedicated you get reserved nodes; on Hosted, warm pools are shared but with isolation guarantees, and you'll see small overhead. we'll quantify in the pricing note.
[00:08:46] Liam: any compliance doc we can send to security?
[00:08:50] Ethan: i'll attach SOC 2 summary, our infra pen test summary, and the Private deployment checklist.
[00:08:58] Sophie: one last bit — during a swap can we annotate logs that show model-version mapping per request for audit?
[00:09:05] Maya: yes each request has model_id and version metadata and we can route logs to your SIEM via the log forwarder.
[00:09:12] Ethan: sweet. i think that's the main set. shall we go through next steps?
[00:09:17] Liam: yes please.
[00:09:20] Ethan: summary/next steps: Maya will run the 24-hour soak for both variants and share heatmaps. i'll send pricing and pilot delta. Atlas to confirm on-call roster and RTO acceptance. we'll schedule a dry-run in staging for emergency swap next week.
[00:09:36] Ravi: thanks, sounds good.
[00:09:40] Sophie: thanks all.
[00:09:43] Ethan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with artifacts.

References mentioned:

- traffic-replay harness (Maya to share link)

End of meeting.

Notes on transcription: there are occasional acronym splits (e.g., "K V cash" for kv cache, "sock two" for SOC 2) and some speaker label mismatches in auto notes. The substance above reflects manual corrections by AE.
